findings.claim: The plan says G1 holds "in every harness APM installs them for", but it does not say who translates the moved agents for OpenCode and Antigravity. APM does not: kmctl plugin patch does it today (opencode.agent_paths/agent_files and antigravity.agents_dir read only kmctl's own _agents plus okf's apm_modules folder). After the move, OpenCode gets APM's raw copies in .opencode/agents/ with Claude front matter. OpenCode drops that front matter silently (the opencode.py docstring, spike:opencode-harness/1), so the agents lose their subagent mode and their tool restriction, and their bodies name mcp__kmaudit__* tools that OpenCode calls by other names. Antigravity loses the translated agents it has today and falls back to the skill's own batch. If kmctl's patch is pointed at kmaudit's agents instead, both translate_agent functions raise PluginError on any mcp__ tool name, because TOOLS maps only Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit and Bash. Having kmctl translate kmaudit's agents would also tie kmaudit's package back to kmctl, which the split is meant to undo. The plan must pick one and say so: kmctl's patch also translates kmaudit's agents from apm_modules, with MCP tool mapping; or kmaudit owns its own translation; or G1 is narrowed to Claude Code agents plus the skill-only path in the other harnesses, with OpenCode's raw agent copies dealt with (removed or left out).

O1's touches leave out kmctl code and tests that name the two agents and will break or go stale after the move: packages/kmctl/tests/test_opencode.py, test_antigravity.py and test_plugin_patch.py (they list kmctl-claims-extractor/kmctl-check-writer as agents the patch writes), the guard-hook test in test_apm_package.py, and the opencode.py/antigravity.py modules whose agent sets change. kmaudit's cli.py help also names the old agents in --by and guard. plan.split reads touches, so the facts must match what the move changes, whichever way p1 is decided.

Resolved: the agents move to a Claude-only sub-package (targets: [claude]), the skills do the batch themselves where no agent exists, and kmctl's translation drops the two agents because it reads only kmctl's own agents_dir() and okf's folder.
Resolved: touches now list opencode.py, antigravity.py, test_opencode.py, test_antigravity.py, test_plugin_patch.py, test_apm_package.py and kmaudit's cli.py.

O1's touches still leave out knowledge that says what this ticket changes. .okf/architecture/overview.md shows the agents as 'Read, Bash; Haiku' in kmctl's package and lists their paths under kmctl's apm/.apm/agents/ (lines 44-47, 324-329, 449-451). .okf/manifesto.md (lines 87-91) says the extractor has 'Read and a shell'. Both become false when the agents move to kmaudit's Claude sub-package with no shell. ADR 0037 and ADR 0040 list the old agent files in their sources front matter, so after the rename kmctl review due reports them as 'source not resolved'. apm-per-package moves these sources to the new paths for the same reason. plan.split reads touches, so add .okf/architecture/overview.md and .okf/manifesto.md, plus the sources of ADR 0037 and 0040, or say why they stay.

The skills' evals were rewritten for the MCP flow but not rerun, so the plan's checked-by item "the skills' evals rerun through skill-creator" and the ticket's done-when (Claude Code's kmaudit-claims-extractor stores claims through the MCP tools with no shell) have no run behind them; the integration test proves install only.
Both results.md files say the tests/test_skills.py checks cover "the agents' tools"; those tools are asserted in packages/kmaudit/tests/test_apm_package.py, not test_skills.py.
